units.title: Sources of Lipids and the Physiology Diagram
units.sec: Sources of Lipids and the Physiology Diagram · p94
units.guide: Hypolipidemic drugs are used in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). The physiology page builds lipid handling from three sources: food entering the small intestine (cholesterol, triglycerides and bile acids, with ezetimibe blocking the NPC1L1 transporter and esterification by ACAT in the epithelial cell), storage in adipose tissue (where niacin blocks the adipocyte and hormone sensitive lipase releases free fatty acids in the fasting state), and synthesis in the liver. Enterohepatic circulation carries bile acids back through the duodenum; VLDL and chylomicrons reach the blood vessel, and the remnants of VLDL and chylomicrons are removed by the liver.

units.title: Cholesterol Synthesis, LDL Receptor Regulation and PCSK9 Drugs
units.sec: Cholesterol Synthesis, LDL Receptor Regulation and PCSK9 Drugs · p95
units.guide: When a cell requires cholesterol it makes it from citrate: ATP citrate lyase converts citrate to acetyl CoA (blocked by bempedoic acid), HMG CoA reductase converts HMG CoA to mevalonic acid (blocked by statins) and the pathway ends in cholesterol for bile acids and steroids. The same cholesterol need upregulates synthesis of the LDL receptor - the effect shared by statins, bempedoic acid, ezetimibe and bile acid binding resins. Plasma LDL reaching the cell is degraded to cholesterol, PCSK9 degrades LDL receptors, alirocumab and evolocumab are monoclonal antibodies against PCSK9, and inclisiran is a siRNA that blocks synthesis of PCSK9. Evinacumab blocks AngPTL-3 to block LPL and lower LDL cholesterol in FHC, while lomitapide is also used in familial hypercholesterolemia.

units.title: Niacin: the Lipoprotein-A Lowering Drug
units.sec: Niacin: the Lipoprotein-A Lowering Drug · p95
units.guide: Niacin is highly toxic and therefore not preferred. It lowers free fatty acids, which lowers TG, VLDL and finally LDL; it is used to lower Lp(a) along with statin plus ezetimibe therapy and gives the maximum increase in HDL (more than statin) although this indication is obsolete. Its side effects are potent hepatotoxicity, insulin resistance progressing to diabetes mellitus and flushing caused by prostaglandin release with vasodilation, for which aspirin is the treatment of choice because it blocks cyclooxygenase and reduces prostaglandin synthesis.

units.title: Triglyceride-lowering Drugs: Omega-3 Fatty Acids, Icosapent and Fibrates
units.sec: Triglyceride-lowering Drugs: Omega-3 Fatty Acids, Icosapent and Fibrates · p96
units.guide: The TG-lowering group contains omega-3 fatty acids, icosapent and fibrates, with fibrates split into halogenated (clofibrate, bezafibrate, fenofibrate) and non-halogenated (gemfibrozil) agents. Icosapent is a derivative of omega-3 fatty acids that blocks release of VLDL by the liver and is used in familial hypertriglyceridemia. Fibrates stimulate PPAR-alpha, which increases LPL synthesis in capillary endothelium, lowering chylomicrons, VLDL, TG and LDL particles; they are DOC in hypertriglyceridemia, chylomicronemia syndrome and type III hyperlipoproteinemia, and fenofibrate also lowers uric acid like febuxostat. Their side effects are myopathy and gall stones, maximal with clofibrate.

units.title: LDL-lowering Drugs: Statins, Bempedoic Acid, Ezetimibe, PCSK9 Inhibitors, Inclisiran and Resins
units.sec: LDL-lowering Drugs: Statins, Bempedoic Acid, Ezetimibe, PCSK9 Inhibitors, Inclisiran and Resins · p96
units.guide: The LDL-lowering indications are ASCVD such as angina, myocardial infarction and stroke, and any patient with raised LDL. The drugs are statins (the DOC, marked as the affordable oral drug class), bempedoic acid (affordable oral drug), ezetimibe (blocks NPC1L1 to reduce cholesterol absorption with upregulation of LDL receptors to lower plasma LDL), PCSK9 inhibitors given as intravenous monoclonal antibodies (evolocumab, alirocumab), inclisiran (small interfering RNA antagonists that block synthesis of PCSK9) and bile acid binding resins.

units.title: Bile Acid Binding Resins
units.guide: Bile acid binding resins are cholestyramine, colesevelam (preferred because of fewer side effects) and colestipol. They inhibit the enterohepatic circulation, so bile acid in the liver falls, cholesterol synthesis rises, demand for cholesterol and LDL rises, LDL receptors increase and plasma LDL finally falls. Their side effects are GI upset (diarrhea/bloating), hypertriglyceridemia, hyperchloremic alkalosis, reduced fat-soluble vitamins E/D/A/K and reduced absorption of other drugs. Uniquely among hypolipidemics they are safe and efficacious as DOC in pregnancy and children, because all other hypolipidemics are contraindicated in pregnancy.

units.title: Statins: Mechanism of Action and Pleiotropic Effects
units.sec: Statins: Mechanism of Action and Pleiotropic Effects · p97
units.guide: Statins save lives by blocking HMG-CoA reductase, an enzyme with maximum activity at night; the resulting effects are lowered LDL, VLDL and TG along with raised HDL and Lp-alpha. Beyond lipid lowering, statins have pleiotropic (non-hypolipidemic) effects: they are anti-aggregant, anti-coagulant, vasodilators through increased release of nitric oxide, antioxidants, anti-inflammatory and they stabilise the atherosclerotic plaque.

units.title: Statin Uses and Pharmacokinetics
units.guide: Statins are DOC in type II hyperlipoproteinemia and are used for ASCVD prophylaxis: primary prophylaxis in those with no prior attack but raised LDL/DM or a history of familial hypercholesterolemia, and secondary prophylaxis when there is a history of angina, MI or stroke. They are absorbed orally and taken up by the liver through OATP1B1; OATP1B1 is blocked by gemfibrozil and clarithromycin, producing statin toxicity, and clarithromycin also blocks glucuronidation and CYP3A4. All statins are CYP3A4 substrates except fluvastatin and rosuvastatin (CYP2C9) and pravastatin, which is excreted unchanged, is best in liver failure and is DOC for protease inhibitor induced dyslipidemia.

units.title: Statin Side Effects, Contraindications and Clinical Applications in ASCVD
units.sec: Statin Side Effects, Contraindications and Clinical Applications in ASCVD · p99
units.guide: Before starting a statin, baseline CPK and LFT are done although monitoring is not required. Side effects are myopathy (increased with fibrates), hepatotoxicity and hyperglycemia; contraindications are pregnancy and children below 11 years (pravastatin below 8 years), and if a fibrate must be combined, fluvastatin is relatively safer. In ASCVD with raised LDL, an LDL of 100-190 mg/dL plus a 10-year ASCVD risk of 5-20% gets a moderate dose statin while a risk above 20% gets a high dose; diabetes with risk below 20% gets moderate dose and 20% or more gets high dose; and clinical ASCVD gets high dose statins. If response is inadequate, ezetimibe or bile acid binding resins (affordable) or inclisiran can be added.

units.title: Management of Hypertriglyceridemia and Familial Hypercholesterolemia
units.sec: Management of Hypertriglyceridemia and Familial Hypercholesterolemia · p100
units.guide: Hypertriglyceridemia is managed according to the risk of ASCVD: when risk is present a statin is tried alone, icosapent is added on an inadequate response and fibrates are then added if the response is still inadequate; when ASCVD risk is absent, fibrates are the DOC for the raised TGs and icosapent is added. Familial hypercholesterolemia is treated with high dose statins as the DOC.
